title: Status
description: Live orchestrator state. Source of truth for /pipeline --resume. current_phase is pattern-validated, not enum-validated: the enum drifted out of sync with the phases the orchestrator actually writes (0.5-map, 2-constraints, 2.5-design, 3-impl-tripwire, ...) and a stale enum derails runs. Canonical values are whatever /pipeline's checkpoint steps write; the pattern only pins the <phase-number>-<slug> shape.

ask_text.description: Truncated, secret-redacted task summary. status.json is committed to git; never let a token-shaped substring through.

risk_tier.description: Copied from spec.json after Phase 1 (post orchestrator tier validation) so checkpoints and re-runs honor the same depth.

panel_roles.description: The Phase 4 panel composition resolved by tier and diff surfaces. Recorded before dispatch so the merge, the rubric, and --resume agree on who was on the panel. design_review is APPENDED TO THIS ARRAY whenever the diff touches a frontend surface, and art_director whenever a visual-contract.json exists for the issue; both also write their own shard, exactly like every other role.

worktree_path.description: OPTIONAL, and preferably OMITTED: no code reads this field from status.json. The Phase 3 worktree path lives in tasks.json, which is where Dev writes it and where the orchestrator, QA and validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs all read it. When present here it is for audit only and MUST be a path RELATIVE to the project root, e.g. .claude/worktrees/42-phase3-20260101-120000 -- never an absolute path, and never a sentence about the path, which is a free-text note in a field typed as a path. WRITER PROHIBITION, and it is a prohibition rather than a promise because nothing redacts this file: status.json is committed AND archived verbatim into the knowledge store, so it must never carry an absolute filesystem path, a command string, or a credential. archive-pipeline.mjs does not read this field as an artifact fallback; the Phase 4 sync step is what preserves worktree artifacts.

phase3_qa_test_commit.description: Architectural tier only: SHA of QA's committed failing-test contract, recorded before Dev dispatches.

review_rounds.description: How many Phase 4 panel rounds this issue has run (the first full panel is 1; each delta re-review adds 1). An EXPLICIT counter because events[] items carry only phase and at, with no round field, so the count cannot be inferred from them.

telemetry.description: Derived, NUMBERS ONLY. Computed from events[] by scripts/pipeline-telemetry.mjs. No note, no path, no command string: this file is archived verbatim.

phase_elapsed_ms.description: Milliseconds spent per phase, keyed by the leading phase LABEL of the event that CLOSED it, resolved through KNOWN_PHASES in scripts/dispatch-model.mjs. events[] entries are EXIT markers -- each carries the `verdict` of the phase it closes, and a verdict is not knowable until that phase has run -- so an interval belongs to the LATER event's phase, not the earlier one. Keys are KNOWN_PHASES tokens and never raw event labels, so an agent-written label can never become a persisted key in this archived file. The token is not always a number: the architectural tier writes 3a and 3b for its two implementation steps, and both are keys here.

total_lead_time_ms.description: Last timed event minus the first. NO `minimum`, deliberately: it is negative when events[] timestamps run backwards, which is a value this repo's own records produce and which the sibling unattributed_ms documents as a supported signal. Forbidding it would be a contract that contradicts its own corpus.

unattributed_ms.description: Milliseconds between events that no phase key could absorb. sum(phase_elapsed_ms) + unattributed_ms == total_lead_time_ms holds by construction, so a phase label this pipeline writes but KNOWN_PHASES does not declare shows up here as a visible number instead of being silently dropped. Negative only when events[] timestamps run backwards, which is itself the signal.

unattributed_events.description: How many event boundaries contributed to unattributed_ms.

untimed_events.description: How many events[] entries were DROPPED before any figure above was computed, because their `at` was unparseable or their `phase` was not a string. Every other number here, total_lead_time_ms INCLUDED, is computed over the surviving events, so the partition balances whether this is 0 or 20 -- a true statement about a population that quietly lost a member. It cannot be folded into unattributed_ms, because an event with no timestamp contributes no duration to attribute, so it is reported as its own count.

attribution.description: Which convention the figures above were computed under. Records written by 0.21.0 or earlier carry no attribution and were computed under the entry-marker convention; treat those figures as historical and stale rather than recomputing them. A closed enum, not free text, because this file is archived verbatim.

effective_config.description: The surface globs and per-role models that were LIVE for this run, so a narrowing is auditable after the fact rather than reconstructable only from a config file that may have changed since. The two migration sets are SEPARATE named entries deliberately: the gate's set REPLACES the defaults and the tripwire's UNIONS with them, and an auditor who cannot tell which was live for which control has learned nothing. An absolute-path glob is recorded as the literal token <absolute-glob-rejected>.

flags.description: One-line-per-agent digest appended after each agent returns; Phase 4 reviewers read this instead of re-parsing earlier artifacts from cold.
